section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces a study investigating the role of self-efficacy generality as a motivational mechanism linking practice variability and transfer of training. The study involved 82 undergraduate students assigned to constant or variable training conditions for a computer decision-making task. Measures of self-efficacy (intensity and generality) and transfer (near and far) were assessed, with results indicating that practice variability increased self-efficacy generality, which in turn influenced far transfer performance and mediated the relationship between practice variability and far transfer.
